title: Shemirat Halashon 29

chapters.title: Speaking to less than three people as a man of truth
chapters.about: Kapetz Chaim chapter 10,issur of lashon hara,reputation for truth

chapters.title: Sins between man and man versus man and God
The danger of speaking when personally involved
Asking for favors and speaking about communities
chapters.about: refusing favors,speaking ill of a whole town,sin of lashon hara

chapters.title: Future benefit and seeking help from influential people
Summary of rules and personal bias

summary: Rabbi Soffer goes through the laws of Shemirat HaLashon from the Hafetz Chaim, focusing on when someone is allowed to speak lashon hara for a constructive purpose without needing three people present. He discusses the differences between sins between man and man versus sins between man and God, and explains the great danger of bias and the desire for revenge when a person is personally involved in the situation.
questions: When is someone allowed to speak lashon hara in front of fewer than three people?
Can you speak lashon hara about someone who committed a sin between man and God if it is for a good purpose?
Why is it so dangerous to tell a negative story when you were personally involved?
What are the specific conditions required to speak out to protect yourself or stop someone from harming you?
